title: A Convertible on a Sunday Drive
description: Identify the parts of an open-top automobile through its folding roof, body fittings, and driver’s controls.
cardDescription: Identify the parts of an open-top automobile through its folding roof, body fittings, and driver’s controls.
subtheme: A Convertible on a Sunday Drive
focus: Convertible describes an automobile with a roof that can be lowered or removed. The clues use ordinary American vehicle words and distinguish a body panel from a driving control.
solvingTip: Picture the car from front to back. A storage lid, a roof feature, and a control inside have different names.
words: Automobile with a roof that can be lowered or removed
Informal name for a car with a folding fabric roof
Shiny metallic finish associated with classic automobile trim
Short name for the panel carrying a car's instruments
American word for a car's rear luggage compartment
American word for the panel covering a car's engine compartment
Cushioned place occupied by a driver or passenger
Safety restraint fastened across an automobile occupant
Sounding device operated by the driver
Circular steering control held by the driver
Short name for a convertible's folding roof
Reflective fitting showing traffic behind the car
Hinged side panel through which a passenger enters

answerNotes.CONVERTIBLE: Convertibles can use fabric tops or folding hardtops, so the name does not require one roof material.
answerNotes.RAGTOP: Ragtop specifically suggests a fabric top, while convertible is the broader vehicle category.
answerNotes.CHROME: Chrome is a surface finish in this setting; it is not the name of the car's whole body material.
answerNotes.DASH: Dash is short for dashboard; the gauges and controls mounted there are individual components.
answerNotes.TRUNK: Trunk names storage space in American English; boot is the familiar British term.

title: Alongside a Yellow School Bus
description: Look at a familiar American school bus through its boarding steps, warning fittings, and passenger layout.
cardDescription: Look at a familiar American school bus through its boarding steps, warning fittings, and passenger layout.
focus: The clues describe recognizable bus features and common vehicle vocabulary. They distinguish the body’s support structure from the seating area and the visible signals around it.
solvingTip: Use a body location or an object’s purpose. A control, a passenger fitting, and a warning display belong to different categories.
words: Passenger vehicle carrying pupils, with spaces omitted
Vehicle framework supporting the body and running equipment
Lamp that repeatedly lights and darkens as a warning
Bar a boarding passenger can grip beside the steps
Passage between the rows of seats in a bus
Color strongly associated with American pupil-transport buses
Reflective fitting helping a bus driver see around the vehicle
One level climbed while boarding the bus
Place where a bus passenger sits
Movable entrance barrier beside the driver
Planned series of stops followed by a bus
Round rolling support beneath the vehicle
Word displayed on a school bus's folding roadside sign

answerNotes.SCHOOLBUS: School bus is written as continuous letters in the grid; it is a vehicle category rather than a single manufacturer.
answerNotes.CHASSIS: A chassis supports the vehicle's major assemblies; the passenger body is built on or integrated with it.
answerNotes.FLASHER: A flasher is a light signal, while a mirror provides a view rather than emitting light.
answerNotes.HANDRAIL: A handrail provides a grip near an entrance; it is not a seat restraint.
answerNotes.AISLE: An aisle allows movement through the passenger area; the steps connect that area with the entrance.

title: A Tractor Beside the Barn
description: Explore the body, controls, and towing fittings of an agricultural tractor.
cardDescription: Explore the body, controls, and towing fittings of an agricultural tractor.
focus: A tractor supplies pulling power and can drive attached equipment. The clues distinguish a towing connection, a rotating power connection, and the driver’s control area.
solvingTip: Start with a large visible part, then look for the smaller connection named by its job.
words: Farm vehicle designed to pull or power working equipment
Connection used to attach a pulled implement to a tractor
Raised pattern on a tractor tire's running surface
Rigid towing bar at the rear of many tractors
Rotating rod that can transmit tractor power to equipment
Large rubber covering around a tractor wheel
Driver's sitting place above the tractor's controls
Panel covering the tractor's engine area
Shaft or assembly supporting the tractor's wheels
Transmission setting selected for a speed or pulling task
Enclosed driver compartment on many farm vehicles
Curved protective panel over a tractor wheel
Machine supplying a tractor's motive power
Soil-turning implement a tractor may pull

answerNotes.TRACTOR: A tractor provides traction and power; it is distinct from the plow, mower, or other implement it operates.
answerNotes.HITCH: A hitch joins the equipment mechanically; a power shaft can serve a separate rotating drive function.
answerNotes.TREAD: Tread helps the tire engage the ground; it differs from the complete tire or wheel.
answerNotes.DRAWBAR: A drawbar provides a pulling attachment, rather than being the whole rear axle.
answerNotes.SHAFT: A power take-off shaft transfers rotation; the hitch itself provides a structural connection.

title: A Hot-Air Balloon at Dawn
description: Name the parts of a hot-air balloon and the plain words describing its shape and movement.
cardDescription: Name the parts of a hot-air balloon and the plain words describing its shape and movement.
focus: A hot-air balloon rises because its heated air is less dense than the surrounding cooler air. Its burner, fabric envelope, and passenger basket are distinct components.
solvingTip: Separate the source of heat from the fabric containing the air and the space carrying passengers.
words: Basket or passenger compartment hanging beneath a balloon
Large fabric body holding the heated air in a balloon
Device supplying heat to a hot-air balloon
Woven material traditionally used for many balloon baskets
Line securing a balloon to a fixed point
Aircraft supported by buoyancy rather than wings
Passenger-carrying container below a hot-air envelope
Visible burning gas above a balloon's heater
Gas mixture heated inside this kind of balloon
Opening through which hot air can be released
To move along with the surrounding wind
Upward supporting effect allowing the balloon to rise
Strong line forming part of balloon handling equipment

answerNotes.GONDOLA: Gondola can name the passenger basket; it also has unrelated meanings in boating and rail travel.
answerNotes.ENVELOPE: Envelope is the balloon's fabric container, not a paper cover for a letter.
answerNotes.BURNER: The burner heats the air; the heated air's lower density contributes to the balloon's lift.
answerNotes.WICKER: Wicker describes woven construction, not one mandatory plant species or fiber.
answerNotes.TETHER: A tether limits movement while attached; free flight is a different operating situation.

title: Riding a Streetcar Downtown
description: Take a short streetcar ride through its seats, fare, bell, and stops along the route.
cardDescription: Take a short streetcar ride through its seats, fare, bell, and stops along the route.
focus: The clues follow a passenger's ride rather than the streetcar's electrical machinery.
solvingTip: Use the boarding and seating words to cross the vehicle's name.
words: Another name for a streetcar running on rails
Printed or electronic proof of a paid streetcar ride
Price paid for the streetcar journey
Pair of rails followed by the streetcar
Ringing device heard on many traditional streetcars
Place where a streetcar passenger sits
Place where the streetcar lets passengers on or off
One long steel strip beneath the streetcar wheels
Glass opening through which a passenger sees downtown
Opening used to board the streetcar
One raised level climbed when boarding an older streetcar
Planned path between the streetcar's stops

answerNotes.TROLLEY: Trolley has several meanings; here it is a passenger vehicle on tracks.
answerNotes.TICKET: A ticket records permission to travel rather than the route itself.
answerNotes.FARE: Fare is the payment, not the name of the destination.
answerNotes.TRACK: The track guides the wheels along the street.
answerNotes.DRIVER: The driver controls the vehicle's movement along its route.
